description: STRENGTHENING AND SUSTAINING NEVADA'S PUBLIC HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE. AFFECTED LOCATIONS: NEVADA (WITHOUT CLARK COUNTY) - THROUGH THE STRENGTHENING U.S. PUBLIC HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE, WORKFORCE, AND DATA SYSTEMS GRANT, THE NEVADA DIVISION OF PUBLIC AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH (DPBH):  - WILL UTILIZE THE WORKFORCE FUNDING TO RETAIN CURRENT STATE EMPLOYEES AND CONTRACTORS FUNDED THROUGH ACADEMIC PARTNERS, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENTS, COMMUNITY PARTNERS, AND NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS.  - TRANSFORM THE OPERATIONS OF THE AGENCY TO ASSURE EFFICIENT WORKFLOWS, IMPROVE TRAINING AND EMPLOYEE SUCCESS, AND COMMIT TO OFFERING MODEL PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES AND QUALITY IMPROVEMENT THROUGH PUBLIC HEALTH ACCREDITATION.  - WILL BE ABLE TO BUILD AN INFECTIOUS DISEASE INFORMATION SYSTEM THAT IS BOTH EFFICIENT AND MODERN. THIS INVESTMENT WILL ALLOW STAFF TO FOCUS ON PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICE DELIVERY INSTEAD OF DUPLICATE DATA ENTRY OR IT SYSTEM FAILURE. ADDITIONALLY, STANDALONE SYSTEMS WILL BE RETIRED FOR A MORE COMPREHENSIVE AND INCLUSIVE EPITRAX DURING THE FIRST YEAR OF THE PROJECT. IN FUTURE YEARS, MORE STAND-ALONE LEGACY SYSTEMS WILL BE RETIRED FOR A MORE COMPREHENSIVE AND ROBUST SINGLE SYSTEM.  AS A RESULT OF THIS AWARD, AND THE OTHER AWARDS PROVIDED BY THE CDC, NEVADA WILL BE BETTER ABLE TO PROACTIVELY PLAN AND PREPARE FOR PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCIES AND RESPOND TIMELIER AND COMPREHENSIVELY TO DAILY AND ONGOING PUBLIC HEALTH NEEDS OF THE DIVERSE COMMUNITIES SERVED.  ACROSS EACH OF THE INVESTMENTS AND PROJECTS UNDER THIS AWARD, DPBH WILL ENSURE THAT DIVERSITY, EQUITY, INCLUSION, AND ACCESSIBILITY ARE CORE FRAMEWORKS CONSIDERED IN EACH AREA.  AS RECOMMENDED, DPBH HAS PREPARED A PROPOSAL TO REFLECT THAT 40% OF THE FUNDS PROJECTED FOR STRATEGY A1: WORKFORCE BE PROVIDED TO THE ALREADY FORMED OR FORMING LOCAL HEALTH AUTHORITIES INCLUDING CARSON CITY HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, WASHOE COUNTY HEALTH DISTRICT, AND THE NEWLY FORMING CENTRAL NEVADA HEALTH DISTRICT. ADDITIONALLY, DPBH WILL BE WORKING WITH THE CDC FOUNDATION, THE UNIVERSITY OF NEVADA, RENO, THE NEVADA ASSOCIATION OF COUNTIES, THE DHHS OFFICE OF MINORITY HEALTH AND EQUITY, AND THE STATE OFFICE OF EPIDEMIOLOGY AS ADDITIONAL SUBCONTRACTORS.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The purpose of the Emerging Infections Programs (EIP) is to assist in local, state, and national efforts to prevent, control, and monitor the public health impact of infectious diseases. The EIP cooperative agreement was formed in 1995 as a key component of CDC’s national strategy to address and reduce emerging infectious disease (EID) threats.  The EIP is a population-based network of state health agencies and their collaborators, including (but not limited to) academic institutions, local health departments, public health and clinical laboratories, infection control professionals, and healthcare providers.   The unique strength of the EIP lies in the network’s ability to quickly translate surveillance and research activities into informed policy and public health practice.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The intent of this program is to fund state, local, and territorial public health departments for HHS Secretarial declared and non-declared public health emergencies having an overwhelming impact on jurisdictional resources. These emergencies require federal support to effectively respond to, manage, and address a significant public health threat. CDC seeks to enhance the Nation’s ability to rapidly mobilize and respond to specific public health crises or emergencies. In addition to immediate response activities, this program provides a mechanism to accelerate readiness for an impending infectious disease threat or other public health crises identified on the event horizon.
